the self-assembled c axis-oriented Bi(2) Sr(3)Co2O(y), thin films were prepared using the sol-gell method and the c axis lattice constant of 15Å, and a phenomenological thermodynamic diagram for the self-assembled orientation is established.

the Bi(2)O(2)(+) layer is the key factor for the self-assembled c-oriented growth.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sol-gel derived thin films with self-assembly c-axis orientation are a good candidate for thermoelectric devices.
the self-assembled c-oriented thin films with misfit structures can be obtained by the sol-gels method, which is very different from the conventional epitaxial thin film growth.

the self-assembled c-oriented films are prepared on different crystallographic orientations of substrates, and the growth of the films on the different substrates is controlled by the same growth mechanism, which is different from that of other complex oxide thin films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c-axis orientation of a thin film is not determined by the orientation of the single crystal substrate.
self-assembled c-oriented thin films can be achieved using chemical solution deposition, and the misfit structure is a key factor to achieve this self-assembled growth.
the misfit structure can be used as a driving force for self-assembled epitaxy.
